review_method: Independent original-pixel inspection of the geological map for all three targets, independently rendered wider regional originals and publication imprint, and park-plan map pages 6 and 9 plus date/authority front matter. Complete source and baseline-rendered rings were viewed. All 179 ordered positions and three complete embedded-map affine registrations were independently recomputed, and both successful acquisition receipts were checked against retained original bytes. Every selected position falls within an inspected original crop. Full outlines, orientation, adjacent distinct waters and material omitted extensions were considered together; neither bounds nor label overlap alone established identity. First observations were recorded before receiving the source researcher verdict. The production decoder was not independently replayed by this reviewer.
counted_unit: Distinct logical inventory lake target IDs; repeated map labels do not increase the target count.

findings.follow_up_scope: No additional work is required for this bounded generalized identity. Complete detailed lake coverage, formal-registry verification, exact adjoining-water boundaries, Korean naming and scalar product application require a separate assessment.
findings.supported_name_scope: The complete selected generalized footprint supports Kississing Lake as a bounded water identity. The island-studded basin, narrow arms and peninsula margins are heavily generalized; several fine northern and southern shoreline extensions are omitted. Islands are not represented as holes. The exact Kississing River transition and complete detailed named-lake extent are not verified. Exact extent and product-name application are not approved.
limits: The island-studded basin, narrow arms and peninsula margins are heavily generalized; several fine northern and southern shoreline extensions are omitted. Islands are not represented as holes. The exact Kississing River transition and complete detailed named-lake extent are not verified.
Kisseynew Lake is separately labelled south beyond the selected ring; Kississing River is river context rather than an alternative lake name.

Official provincial geological and park cartography supports the stated associations. One provincial-government publisher group provides two publications; independence of underlying hydrographic datasets and formal naming-registry authority are unverified.
No Korean form or additional whole-lake alias is certified; registered overlays do not establish exact shores or naming partitions.
